assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale measurement of intergenerational mobility has transformed evidence on inequality of opportunity and its geographic variation.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman are central to the linked-data research program; the breadth of the collaboration complicates a fully exhaustive allocation of credit.
assessment.maturity: The empirical approach and findings are extensively developed and influential across public and labour economics.
uncertainties: The candidate description combines a broad research program with contributions by several closely associated scholars.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence designs supplied unusually direct, consequential evidence on labour-market discrimination and set a durable empirical standard.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are especially central to the canonical résumé-correspondence contribution, while Charles represents the wider research area.
assessment.maturity: The design has been replicated, extended and integrated into mainstream labour-market research over decades.
uncertainties: The extent to which a prize should recognize a design family rather than its most influential applications remains uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work substantially sharpened understanding of how trade and technology shocks affect local labour demand, wages and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson form a coherent credited group for the trade-shock and task-based empirical program.
assessment.maturity: The research has generated a large literature and has had sustained influence on labour, trade and policy debates.
uncertainties: Separating the lasting contribution of trade shocks from the broader task-and-technology literature is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The modern analysis of monopsony has changed how economists interpret wage setting, employer power and labour-market policy.
assessment.attribution: Manning is a foundational synthesizer and theorist of modern monopsony; the credited contribution also reflects important empirical and later theoretical work by others.
assessment.maturity: Its implications have been extensively tested and are now central to labour economics.
uncertainties: Credit is diffuse across foundational theory, empirical measurement and recent policy-oriented advances.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on early-life health and conditions established their central role in human-capital formation and later economic outcomes.
assessment.attribution: Currie and Almond are leading contributors to the empirical early-life-conditions literature, with Cunha central to its skill-formation dimension.
assessment.maturity: A long and diverse body of evidence has made early-life interventions a core issue in applied economics.
uncertainties: The candidate joins related but distinct strands on health shocks and dynamic skill formation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Empirical analysis of taxable-income responses has materially informed optimal-tax theory, revenue estimation and policy design.
assessment.attribution: Saez and Slemrod are central to the elasticity-of-taxable-income framework, while Chetty and Stantcheva represent important related developments.
assessment.maturity: The framework is well established and influential in both public-finance research and practical tax analysis.
uncertainties: Elasticity estimates can be sensitive to institutional context, avoidance responses and identification choices.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The integration of theory and data on selection in insurance markets has improved understanding of market failures and insurance policy.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein and Einav are prominent empirical contributors, with Salanie a major theoretical and econometric contributor to the broader area.
assessment.maturity: The field has produced sustained empirical findings across health and other insurance markets.
uncertainties: The proposed contribution spans distinct theoretical and empirical approaches rather than one singular discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods became foundational tools for credible estimation with persistent outcomes and individual effects.
assessment.attribution: Arellano and Bond are directly identified with the canonical estimator; Blundell made a major extension through system GMM.
assessment.maturity: The methods have been widely used, scrutinized and refined across applied economics for many years.
uncertainties: Their ubiquity does not eliminate concerns about weak instruments, specification and misuse in applications.
